correctness.rationale: Independently integrated derivatives of the reference quadratic Lagrange basis (the products are quadratic, hence the Lobatto rule is exact here), used the basis integrals for the nodal quadrature weights, assembled before boundary restriction, and inverted the entire polynomial matrix 18tS(t) over Z[t] by characteristic-polynomial arithmetic, without parity blocks or the frozen script. Verified the 625 entries and their 55 reflection/exchange/transposition classes. The exact recalculation found 45 zero-variation and 10 one-variation classes, positive denominator coefficients up to allowed zeros, and strictly positive numerator constants. Only the (1,3) orbit is negative at 21/5; every other numerator is strictly positive there, hence positive throughout (0,21/5] by Descartes' rule, including multiplicities. The recomputed witness is the stated -3Q divided by the stated positive denominator. Q has one sign variation and opposite signs at 41999/10000 and 21/5, so its only positive root is simple. At that root the eight witness entries alone vanish, and at every larger t the witness is negative. The rational value at 5 and the displayed root digits agree. S is SPD by the Dirichlet energy with a positive diagonal 1D mass and SPD 1D stiffness. Right multiplication by M_2 preserves signs. This is exactly the stated homogeneous Dirichlet nodal inverse criterion, not a general boundary or time-stepping result.
residual_risks: The proof uses exact finite polynomial arithmetic plus a global sign argument, not a formal proof-assistant certificate. The decimal root is illustrative.

evidence: The frozen necessity is a particular Green-entry numerator changing sign once; sufficiency and the boundary require signs of all other Green entries. A sufficient mesh criterion cannot provide this necessity, and a single sampled counterexample on another mesh cannot classify the continuous parameter on this mesh.
The periodic backward-Euler matrix has a different discrete operator and includes a time-step parameter; its exact positivity criterion does not imply the spatial inverse theorem.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The finite symbolic classification, including its exact equality case, is the distinct claim, not Q² inverse positivity as a concept or loss of positivity on graded grids as a phenomenon.

evidence: Inverse nonnegativity is equivalent to preservation of nonnegative discrete nodal loads. Since the quadrature mass is diagonal and strictly positive, switching between the stiffness Green matrix and the mass-inverted operator cannot change any sign.

value.rationale: This is a natural graded family with a single interior element adjustable independently of overall rescaling, and with a nontrivial discrete monotonicity issue even though stiffness remains SPD. The exact interval, complete critical zero pattern and rational failure witness are useful as a graded-mesh benchmark and distinguish a genuinely sharp limit from conservative sufficient mesh bounds. The value is not a claim of new general finite-element convergence or stability theory.
residual_risks: Exact cutoff applies to the one-parameter symmetric three-element family only.
